economics.trade-define1.0004.all: When a country can produce more of a good than another country using the same resources (or the same output with fewer resources).

economics.trade-define2.0003.all: When countries concentrate on producing the goods/services they are best at (lowest opportunity cost) (1) and trade with other countries for the rest (1).

economics.trade-describe.0008.all: Domestic firms face competition from cheaper imports (1) and may close, causing unemployment (1). (Alt: infant industries cannot grow; over-dependence on imports.)

economics.trade-explain.0012.all: Cheaper imported steel takes market share (1), so domestic steel firms lose revenue and may close (1), causing structural unemployment among steel workers in Novaris (1).

economics.trade-mcq-auth.0002.all: a lower opportunity cost than other countries

economics.trade-mcq-def.0004.all: When a country can produce more of a good than another country using the same resources

economics.trade-state.0002.all: To obtain goods it cannot produce itself / to benefit from specialisation and comparative advantage / lower prices / greater choice.

economics.trade-state-class.0003.all: Domestic firms may close due to foreign competition causing unemployment / infant industries cannot develop / over-dependence on imports.

economics.trade-state-id.0008.all: a disadvantage of free trade for a country

economics.unemployment-analyse-1.0006.all: Structural unemployment: skills mismatch (688,000 vacancies unfilled) - occupational immobility; geographical immobility (travel help suggests jobs in other areas); persistent 5.5% shows not cyclical; possibly frictional; result: vacancies coexist with unemployment.

economics.unemployment-analyse-2.0007.all: Cyclical unemployment 4.0%->7.5%: lower incomes -> lower consumption/AD -> multiplier, further job losses; govt spends more on benefits, less tax revenue -> budget deficit; lost output (inside PPC); social costs, deskilling; construction/retail regions hit hard; lower inflation.

economics.unemployment-assess-1.0007.all: For: training addresses skills mismatch/occupational immobility, fills 829,000 vacancies, raises productivity. Against: time lags, cost/opportunity cost, may not match employers' needs, geographical immobility needs travel/housing help, other causes. Judgement: combined with travel help best.

economics.unemployment-assess-2.0004.all: For: recession -> cyclical unemployment; higher G raises AD, multiplier effect, construction projects directly hire construction workers; Against: budget deficit/debt, time lags, inflation, crowding out, alternative of interest rate cuts. Judgement depends on fiscal position and size of output gap.

economics.unemployment-data.0016.a: 1,592,924/17,831,000 x 100 = 8.93% (note: conflicts with 7.5% in Extract A)
economics.unemployment-data.0016.b: Lower incomes -> lower consumption/AD -> multiplier; benefits up, tax revenue down -> deficit; lost output; social costs; construction/retail hit.
economics.unemployment-data.0016.c: For higher G: raises AD, multiplier, infrastructure creates construction jobs. Against: debt, time lags, inflation, crowding out, other policies (interest rates). Supported judgement.

economics.unemployment-define1.0001.all: When people of working age who are willing and able to work and actively seeking work are without a paid job.

economics.unemployment-define2.0007.all: Unemployment that occurs at certain times of the year (1) because demand for some jobs varies with the seasons, e.g. tourism, farming (1).

economics.unemployment-describe.0010.all: Lower consumer incomes reduce demand for firms' products (1), lowering sales revenue and profit (1).

economics.unemployment-evaluate-1.0004.all: For: skills mismatch shown by 841,000 vacancies; retraining reduces occupational immobility, raises productivity, LRAS. Against: time lags, cost, training may not fit needs, geographical immobility, demand-side issues. Judgement: training plus mobility help is best; depends on quality and employer links.

economics.unemployment-evaluate-2.0001.all: For: recession, cyclical unemployment 5.2%->8.5%; G raises AD, multiplier, construction projects. Against: debt, lags, inflation, crowding out, alternatives (interest rate cuts, tax cuts). Judgement depends on fiscal space and recession depth.

economics.unemployment-explain.0009.all: Seasonal unemployment (1): hotel workers lose jobs when demand for tourism falls in winter (1), so Lyon hotel staff are unemployed for those 4 months each year (1).

economics.unemployment-mcq-class.0007.all: Construction workers laid off during a recession

economics.unemployment-mcq-def.0002.all: The percentage of the labour force that is unemployed

economics.unemployment-state.0001.all: Loss of income / lower living standards / loss of skills / stress or ill health.

economics.unemployment-state-class.0004.all: Workers laid off during a recession due to falling demand (e.g. construction workers).
